critiques.assumption: An order-specific map can independently establish both inventory correctness and the intended arrangement when it also supplies the checking template.
critiques.limitation: A mistaken map could agree perfectly with a mistaken kit. Silhouette checking would then establish internal consistency while dispatching the wrong ordered arrangement. D2-O3 supports investigating contents errors, but supplies no evidence that this common-source failure occurred.
critiques.opening: Keep the shared inventory/assembly surface, but derive its acceptance check directly from the original order slip and existing cutting templates.
critiques.comparison: Physical completeness checking alone counts what its template expects; layout instruction alone guides placement. A1 combines these benefits through one surface, but also couples their errors. An independent order-to-template check could retain that interaction while detecting shared specification mistakes. It fails if the second check merely copies the map, if the original order is wrong, or if checking consumes the time saving.
critiques.probe: Challenge reusable sample kits with known, deliberately introduced map/parts discrepancies and self-consistent wrong map/kit pairs; compare detection with and without direct order-slip checking. These are proposed tests, not observed failures.

openings.claim: Hypothesis: independently validating each layout map against its order before using that map for kit checking prevents a shared map error from becoming an undetected packing error.
openings.delta: Adds an independent source of correctness to A1 rather than another check against the same possibly mistaken representation.
openings.prediction: Direct order-derived checks detect more self-consistent wrong kits than map-only checks, while correct kits remain straightforward for customers to assemble.
openings.probe: Within the 15-sample allowance, use balanced correct and seeded-error kits across compartment counts and colors; counterbalance worker/check order and conceal seeded status. Record detection, false alarms, and total preparation/checking/packing time. Correct every seeded kit before ten participants test the resulting maps unaided. Separately retain A1 fit and transport probes. Price added work/materials before adoption; these samples cannot establish the 60-order success thresholds.
assumptions: Original order slips accurately encode accepted choices.
Independent checking fits available working time, the fixed delivery date, and both cost limits.
Footprint, capacity, reversible partitions, selected counts and colors remain unchanged.
